The Old Jewish Quarter

Ghetto · Manduria, Italy

Certain news about the Jewish presence in Manduria (once called Casalnovo) starts in the 12 -15 th centuries. Since 1648 mention is made to the ‘Jewish Ghetto’ established by city Mayor Filippo Bianchetti. The area still maintains its original name: it extends around vico Stretto, vico Lacaita and vico degli Ebrei and can be accessed by three entrances marked by arches, one of which bears the date, 1602. It is a rectangular shaped area characterised by a maze of alleys and lanes with gates giving access to each house directly off the street.
